sa_market_summary: The Hyundai i20 is one of the most popular compact hatchbacks in South Africa, competing directly with the VW Polo. It offers excellent value for money, generous standard equipment, and low running costs. The second generation i20 (2015-2019) established strong reliability credentials, and the third generation (2020+) added modern technology. Hyundai's 5-year/100,000km warranty on new vehicles transfers to the first used buyer, making certified pre-owned examples especially attractive. Parts are widely available at Hyundai dealers and independent motor spares shops.

known_faults.description: The turbocharged 1.0 T-GDi three-cylinder engine can experience turbocharger wear if oil change intervals are not strictly observed. The small turbo operates at higher temperatures relative to its size.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check for blue smoke under acceleration. Listen for turbo whine. Verify strict oil change history (every 10,000km or annually with correct 5W-30 oil).
known_faults.source: Hyundai SA technical reports, SA independent workshop data

known_faults.description: The infotainment system on 2015-2019 i20 models can freeze or reboot intermittently. Hyundai SA has released software updates for most affected units.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Test infotainment on startup and confirm it boots within 30 seconds. Request a software update record.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R0 (software update at dealer) to R4,000 (unit replacement)
known_faults.source: Hyundai SA service bulletins, owner community reports

known_faults.description: Three-cylinder engines have an inherent vibration at idle. The i20 1.0 T-GDi exhibits more vibration than four-cylinder alternatives. This is a characteristic, not a defect, but can be disconcerting.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Evaluate idle vibration levels personally and decide if it is acceptable. Check if engine mounts have been replaced ,  worn mounts worsen the vibration.
known_faults.source: SA owner reports, Cars.co.za i20 reviews

known_faults.description: AC compressor failure reported on higher mileage 2015-2017 i20 models. A clicking noise from the AC compressor when activated is the early warning sign.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Test air conditioning performance ,  it should cool the cabin within 60 seconds on a hot day. Listen for any compressor rattle or clicking.
known_faults.source: SA AC specialist workshops, Hyundai SA owner forums

what_to_inspect_before_buying: Verify remaining Hyundai warranty coverage ,  5-year/100,000km if still within limits
Check infotainment for freezing and request software update history
Inspect for rust on lower door edges and sills (particularly older 2015-2016 models)
Test all electric windows and mirrors
Request full Hyundai SA service history with dealer stamps
Check tyre condition and size ,  non-standard tyres void warranty claims
owner_sentiment: Positive. i20 owners appreciate the value proposition and low running costs. The 5-year warranty is a strong selling point for first-time buyers. Main concerns are the 1.0 T-GDi vibration and reliability of the infotainment on older models. Hyundai SA after-sales service is generally rated well.
